title: Geneticists
description: Research and study the inheritance of traits at the molecular, organism or population level. May evaluate or treat patients with genetic disorders.

tasks.text: Plan or conduct basic genomic and biological research related to areas such as regulation of gene expression, protein interactions, metabolic networks, and nucleic acid or protein complexes.
Evaluate genetic data by performing appropriate mathematical or statistical calculations and analyses.
Analyze determinants responsible for specific inherited traits, and devise methods for altering traits or producing new traits.
Evaluate, diagnose, or treat genetic diseases.
Create or use statistical models for the analysis of genetic data.
Verify that cytogenetic, molecular genetic, and related equipment and instrumentation is maintained in working condition to ensure accuracy and quality of experimental results.
Design sampling plans or coordinate the field collection of samples such as tissue specimens.
Conduct family medical studies to evaluate the genetic basis for traits or diseases.
Search scientific literature to select and modify methods and procedures most appropriate for genetic research goals.
Review, approve, or interpret genetic laboratory results.
Attend clinical and research conferences and read scientific literature to keep abreast of technological advances and current genetic research findings.
Extract deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or perform diagnostic tests involving processes such as gel electrophoresis, Southern blot analysis, and polymerase chain reaction analysis.
Confer with information technology specialists to develop computer applications for genetic data analysis.
Design and maintain genetics computer databases.
Participate in the development of endangered species breeding programs or species survival plans.
Plan curatorial programs for species collections that include acquisition, distribution, maintenance, or regeneration.
Prepare results of experimental findings for presentation at professional conferences or in scientific journals.
Maintain laboratory notebooks that record research methods, procedures, and results.
Write grants and papers or attend fundraising events to seek research funds.
Develop protocols to improve existing genetic techniques or to incorporate new diagnostic procedures.
Supervise or direct the work of other geneticists, biologists, technicians, or biometricians working on genetics research projects.
Collaborate with biologists and other professionals to conduct appropriate genetic and biochemical analyses.
Instruct medical students, graduate students, or others in methods or procedures for diagnosis and management of genetic disorders.
Maintain laboratory safety programs and train personnel in laboratory safety techniques.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension

skills.name: Writing

skills.name: Speaking

skills.name: Critical Thinking

skills.name: Active Learning

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Monitoring

skills.name: Instructing

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Coordination

skills.name: Persuasion

skills.name: Negotiation

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C++, Microsoft Visual C# .NET, Oracle Java, Perl.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Bioinformatics databases, Database software, HapMap, Microsoft Access.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Linux, UNIX.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Basic Local Alignment Search Tool BLAST, ClustalW, Deoxyribonucleic acid DNA sequence analysis software, Insightful S-PLUS.

skills.name: File versioning software
skills.def: Software to archive and track edits to files for comparison and reference. Examples: Git.

skills.name: Application server software
skills.def: Software to support or run applications which provide services through a communication protocol. Examples: GitHub.
